articles.title: System Overview
articles.summary: A plain-language map of the platform so you know where to go for each task.
faq: Where should I spend most of my time day to day
Which sections are for trading versus system maintenance
content: Use Dashboard for live monitor control, bankroll/portfolio view, and quick status checks.
Use Trade Monitor when you want detailed per-monitor state, active trade context, and settings.
Use Account views for balances, transfer context, and historical outcomes over time.
Use System/Operations views only when diagnosing issues or managing service health.

articles.title: Dashboard Layout and Navigation
articles.summary: What each major dashboard area does and how to move through routine workflows.
faq: What is the fastest way to find a specific monitor
Why does the panel value change when I switch tabs
content: Top panel: switch between Portfolio, Bankroll, and PnL tabs to change what value and chart are shown.
View buttons (1d/1w/1m/1y/all) only change the time window, not the underlying account state.
Monitor tiles show each monitor's current status and core stats, while list view favors scanning many monitors quickly.
Use the search/filter controls first when troubleshooting monitor behavior to avoid changing the wrong monitor.

articles.title: Monitor Management
articles.summary: How to create, enable, pause, and tune monitors safely.
faq: What is the difference between deactivating and disabling auto-trade
When should I use paper trade mode
content: Activate/deactivate controls whether the monitor is in the live rotation.
Auto-trade controls execution behavior for that monitor while it is active.
Paper trade mode keeps logic running but prevents live execution so you can validate behavior safely.
Change one setting at a time and observe at least one full cycle before making additional tuning changes.

articles.title: Allocation and Bankroll Controls
articles.summary: How monitor allocation percentages and bankroll values affect behavior.
faq: Why does monitor allocation not match expected dollar amount immediately
Does changing allocation rewrite history
content: Allocation percentages define how much of available strategy capital each monitor can use.
Bankroll values represent current baseline capital used for performance and sizing context.
Allocation edits affect future behavior; they do not rewrite previously recorded trades.
After major allocation changes, verify monitor status and expected position sizing before re-enabling full automation.

articles.title: Account and History Views
articles.summary: How to read balances, PnL, and historical data correctly.
faq: Which value is cash versus total portfolio
Why do some history views update after new fills settle
content: Portfolio includes current account context used by the dashboard portfolio panel.
Bankroll reflects current strategy base context used for risk and return framing.
PnL view is cumulative over the selected time window and can differ from point-in-time cash changes.
Use day/week/month/year windows to answer specific questions instead of comparing all windows at once.

articles.title: Automated Trade Lifecycle
articles.summary: What happens from signal detection through entry, management, and exit.
faq: What conditions must be true before an entry can fire
Why would a monitor skip an otherwise valid-looking setup
content: A monitor evaluates market conditions and strategy thresholds before attempting entry.
Once active, state transitions move through entry checks, execution attempts, and trade management.
Exits occur by strategy logic, risk controls, or explicit stop conditions.
Final outcomes are reflected in history and performance views after synchronization completes.

articles.title: Live Trade Monitoring and Statuses
articles.summary: How to interpret monitor statuses, cooldowns, and transitions in real time.
faq: What does cooldown mean in practice
Why can status appear to move quickly between states
content: Status labels describe where the monitor is in its current decision or execution cycle.
Cooldown indicates a temporary block before the monitor is allowed to re-enter.
Brief status changes can be normal when data and execution updates arrive close together.
Investigate only if a state remains stuck longer than expected for that strategy.

articles.title: How Real-Time Updates Work
articles.summary: What should update instantly, what updates on read, and what to expect during load.
faq: Why can I see a short delay before a panel updates
How do I tell delay from stale data
content: Most dashboard values update when change events arrive and the UI re-queries the latest data.
A short delay can happen during busy periods, but values should converge to the latest recorded state.
Switching tabs should not change the underlying account state; it only changes what slice is visible.
If one panel is stale while others update, treat that as a targeted issue rather than a full system outage.

articles.title: Stale or Unexpected Values
articles.summary: A practical checklist when values appear frozen, delayed, or inconsistent.
faq: What should I check first when a panel stops updating
How do I confirm if the issue is display-only
content: First, confirm whether the issue affects one panel or the entire dashboard.
Check whether monitor statuses and other live metrics are still moving; this separates UI-only from broader issues.
If only portfolio/bankroll appears stale, compare against the latest known account snapshot and reload the page once.
If stale behavior persists after restart or page reload, escalate with timestamped examples and affected panels.

articles.title: Monitor Not Firing Entries
articles.summary: Why a monitor may stay idle and how to check gating settings quickly.
faq: Can cooldown alone block entries
Do paper-trade settings affect live auto-trade behavior
content: Verify monitor is active and auto-trade is enabled for the intended mode.
Check cooldown and threshold settings first; these are common entry blockers.
Confirm allocation and bankroll context are sufficient for expected position sizing.
Review recent status transitions to identify where the decision flow is stopping.

articles.title: Restart and Health Checks
articles.summary: Safe restart flow and the minimum checks before returning to normal operation.
faq: What must be verified immediately after restart
When is it safe to resume normal trading behavior
content: Restart services through the standard supervised flow, not ad-hoc process kills.
Verify core pages load and key account/monitor values return expected data.
Confirm real-time updates are flowing before declaring recovery complete.
Only resume full operation after both service health and user-facing behavior look normal.

articles.title: Deployment Safety Baseline
articles.summary: How to deploy with low risk and quickly validate production behavior.
faq: What are the must-pass checks right after deploy
What should trigger rollback consideration
content: Use a consistent pre-deploy and post-deploy checklist for every release.
Validate monitor controls, account panels, and real-time updates first because they are most user-visible.
Capture a short verification note after each deployment for future troubleshooting context.
If core workflows fail or values are clearly wrong, pause and stabilize before further changes.
